narrativeReportMd:
# UsageContext R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No local hard instance-breaking structural change was found for `UsageContext`. The datatype still has the same local elements, cardinalities, choice datatypes, reference targets, modifier flags, summary flags, and element definitions. The material local migration concerns are terminology-related: the `code` binding moved its value set canonical from the FHIR namespace to THO, and the example `value[x]` value set composition changed.

## Scope
This assessment is limited to the assigned `UsageContext` datatype and its directly referenced binding value sets/code systems available in the local R4 and R6 packages. Inherited `Element` and `DataType` changes, including the root baseDefinition shift from `Element` to `DataType`, are explicitly out of scope.

## Main migration themes
R4 instances with `code` and one `value[x]` should remain structurally valid under the R6 datatype. Implementers should review terminology package availability, enum generation, validator configuration, value-set expansion caches, and business rules that assume the R4 `usage-context-type` or `use-context` compositions.

## Highest-impact findings
There are no Critical or High findings. The two findings are Low-impact terminology/runtime risks rather than hard JSON/XML representation breaks.

## Findings requiring human review
Both terminology findings deserve human review if a system enforces or generates code lists from binding value sets. The R6 `UsageContext.code` binding targets an external THO ValueSet not present in the local R6 core package, and neither relevant value set was expanded against a terminology server.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The terminology moves are probably part of normal FHIR/THO governance and value-set evolution, but compatibility would have been easier if the R6 package included explicit aliases, redirects, or cross-version ConceptMaps for the old FHIR value-set canonical and the changed `use-context` compose.

## Follow-up analysis
The base `DataType`/`Element` hierarchy and inherited constraints should be assessed in their own reports. A terminology-focused review should compare current THO expansions for `usage-context-type` and `use-context`, including whether `agreement-scope` is now an intended `UsageContext.code`.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No local hard instance-breaking `UsageContext` structure change was found. The main concerns are the `code` binding canonical move to THO and the changed example `use-context` value set composition; confidence is limited mainly by missing R6 THO terminology and expansions.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is primarily about terminology infrastructure, not transforming the datatype shape. Existing JSON/XML paths remain `code` and one `value[x]`, with the same allowed choice datatypes and reference target profiles. Validators and generated models should be checked for hard-coded value-set canonicals, bundled R4 terminology, expansion caches, and application rules that interpret `UsageContext.code` or offer UI pick lists for `UsageContext.valueCodeableConcept`.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for local StructureDefinition shape because both snapshots and differentials were compared directly. Overall confidence is Medium because the R6 `usage-context-type` ValueSet is external to the local R6 core package and no terminology expansions or official change notes were available.

findings.title: UsageContext.code extensible binding value set canonical moved to terminology.hl7.org

oldState.summary: `UsageContext.code` was `1..1 Coding` with an extensible binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/usage-context-type`.

binding.description: A code that specifies a type of context being specified by a usage context.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R4 local ValueSet includes all codes from `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/usage-context-type`; the local R4 CodeSystem contains `gender`, `age`, `focus`, `user`, `workflow`, `task`, `venue`, `species`, and `program`.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, the binding value-set canonical was in the FHIR namespace and the referenced ValueSet/CodeSystem were bundled in the R4 core package.

newState.summary: `UsageContext.code` remains `1..1 Coding` with extensible strength, but the binding value set is now `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/usage-context-type`.

binding.description: A code that specifies a type of context being specified by a usage context.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: No `ValueSet-usage-context-type.json` or `CodeSystem-usage-context-type.json` was found in the local R6 core package. The binding therefore depends on an external THO terminology artifact for exact expansion and possible added/changed codes.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, the binding points at the THO ValueSet canonical. The element shape and binding strength did not change, but local core-package resolution behavior changes for validators and code generators.

facts.note: The conformance strength is unchanged; the risk is canonical resolution and possible terminology content drift.

facts.oldValue: R4 core package contains ValueSet-usage-context-type.json and CodeSystem-usage-context-type.json.
facts.newValue: R6 core package does not contain a local usage-context-type ValueSet or CodeSystem file.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id and path are unchanged (`UsageContext.code`), and the datatype/cardinality/flags are otherwise identical.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a direct instance-shape break: `code` is still a required `Coding`, and extensible bindings do not make every out-of-set code invalid. The practical risk is runtime/tooling behavior. Validators, terminology caches, generated enum metadata, or business rules that resolve the R4 FHIR value-set canonical from the core package may fail or warn differently in R6 unless THO terminology is installed. R6-to-R4 representability is low risk structurally, but semantic review is needed if R6 permits new usage-context type codes that R4 terminology did not know.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Misinterpreting or dropping usage-context categories can affect artifact selection and filtering, but no direct clinical data element is removed or made invalid by this change alone.

justification.inferredGoal: Move externally governed terminology to THO canonical locations while keeping the `UsageContext.code` datatype contract unchanged.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base R6 element design is applicable because the `code` shape and extensible binding strength remain R4-compatible; aliases, redirects, or ConceptMaps would be terminology compatibility aids rather than base-model alternatives.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving externally governed terminology to THO is a reasonable R6 terminology-governance goal, and the change does not remove or rename `UsageContext.code`, alter its `Coding` type, or strengthen the extensible binding. Existing R4 instances remain structurally valid in R6; the residual breakage is limited to terminology-resolution, enum-generation, and cache behavior for systems that depended on the old FHIR value-set canonical.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The backward-compatible alternative question is not applicable as a base-design judgment because this finding is not an R4-to-R6 instance-shape break. A bundled alias, redirect, or ConceptMap from `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/usage-context-type` to the THO canonical would reduce migration friction for validators and code generators, but that is a compatibility mitigation and would also prolong duplicate canonical support.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Terminology aliases or redirects reduce tooling friction but add duplicate canonical handling and do not change the base R6 datatype design.

evidence.detail: R4 `UsageContext.code` binding value set is `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/usage-context-type` with extensible strength.
R6 `UsageContext.code` binding value set is `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/usage-context-type` with extensible strength.
The R4 local CodeSystem contains nine usage-context type codes: `gender`, `age`, `focus`, `user`, `workflow`, `task`, `venue`, `species`, and `program`.
No R6 core package file matching `*usage-context-type*.json` was found.

examples.examplesMd: No JSON instance transform is required for the canonical change itself. A representative risk is an R6 validator or generated enum resolver that cannot resolve `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/usage-context-type` because only the R4 core package terminology was installed.

findings.narrativeMd: `UsageContext.code` kept its local element contract but changed the value-set canonical from the R4 FHIR namespace to THO. That can surprise systems that treat binding canonicals as stable identifiers for enum generation, pick lists, cached expansions, or validation package loading. The change is not a hard instance break because the JSON/XML element is still a `Coding` and the binding strength remains extensible.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance does not become R6-invalid solely because of this canonical change. However, validators that enforce or resolve extensible bindings may produce different warnings or fail terminology resolution if they lack the THO package. In the reverse direction, R6 instances using new THO usage-context type codes, if any, are structurally representable in R4 as `Coding` but may not be recognized as in the R4 extensible value set.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Install the appropriate THO terminology package or configure a terminology server when validating R6. Audit code generators and enum/pick-list builders for hard-coded `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/usage-context-type`. If cross-version validation matters, compare the R4 and current THO expansions and add mappings or warnings for codes present only in one version.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change appears probably justified as a terminology-governance move, but it could have been less disruptive with a bundled alias, explicit redirect, or ConceptMap preserving the old value-set canonical as a compatibility entry point. Without that, offline consumers must discover and install the external terminology artifact.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The exact R6 `usage-context-type` expansion was not available locally. Review against current THO before classifying specific code additions or removals.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 and R6 keep `UsageContext.code` as a required `Coding` with an extensible binding. The confirmed change is the binding value set canonical moving from the FHIR core URL to `terminology.hl7.org`; the R4 value set already points at the THO `usage-context-type` CodeSystem, so existing instances using codes such as `gender`, `age`, or `workflow` do not need a wire-format change. The practical risk is an R6 terminology loader or validator that has only the old core-package terminology and cannot resolve the new canonical, which is resolver/package churn rather than a path-level data compatibility break.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition `UsageContext.code`: min 1, max 1, type `Coding`, extensible binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/usage-context-type`.
R6 StructureDefinition `UsageContext.code`: same cardinality and type, extensible binding to `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/usage-context-type`.
R4 `ValueSet/usage-context-type` includes `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/usage-context-type`, and the R4 CodeSystem defines the expected context-type codes.
The R6 core package has no bundled `*usage-context-type*.json` artifact, so offline tooling may need THO terminology resolution.
freshReview.fmmEffect: The supplied R4 maturity context is trial-use with unknown standards status, which softens stability pressure compared with normative content. Even without that softening, this is not a direct instance-validity break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: metadata/tooling: binding canonical resolution changes; existing `Coding` instances remain structurally valid and the extensible binding does not by itself make prior codings invalid.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A compatibility alias, redirect, or bundled legacy value set could reduce resolver friction, but keeping the old canonical as the base R6 binding would conflict with the terminology-governance move and create duplicate canonical entry points. That is useful packaging support, not a clearly better base StructureDefinition design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: I agree with the existing report's low/non-hard impact direction, but I would not treat the alias or redirect idea as strong evidence of a less-breaking base R6 design.

findings.title: UsageContext.value[x] example value set composition changed

oldState.summary: `UsageContext.value[x]` was `1..1` with choices `CodeableConcept`, `Quantity`, `Range`, or `Reference`, and an example binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/use-context`.

binding.description: A code that defines the specific value for the context being specified.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R4 compose included `usps-state`, `practitioner-specialty`, SNOMED practice setting and species filters, ISO 3166, M49 regions, administrative gender, condition-code, NUCC provider taxonomy, v3 ActEncounterCode, and v3 ActTaskCode.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, the bound example ValueSet was draft, non-experimental, titled `ConformanceUseContext`, and had a broader compose with `usps-state` and `practitioner-specialty` includes.

newState.summary: `UsageContext.value[x]` has the same datatype choices, cardinality, reference targets, example binding strength, and value-set canonical, but the R6 `use-context` ValueSet compose changed.

binding.description: A code that defines the specific value for the context being specified.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 compose removes the R4 `usps-state` and `practitioner-specialty` includes, uses `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/v2-0265`, removes a duplicate ISO 3166 include, and adds `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/usage-context-agreement-scope`.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, the `use-context` ValueSet is still draft and example-bound but is now experimental and includes a new agreement-scope value set whose codes are intended for `UsageContext.valueCodeableConcept` when the usage-context type is agreement scope.

facts.note: The canonical is unchanged; the referenced ValueSet's compose changed.

facts.field: R4 compose includes absent from R6 compose
R6 compose includes absent from R4 compose

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id, path, choice types, binding canonical, and binding strength are unchanged; the change is in the referenced `use-context` ValueSet artifact.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because the binding strength is `example`, base FHIR validation should not reject an instance merely because its `valueCodeableConcept` coding is outside the example ValueSet. The practical effects are semantic and runtime: generated pick lists, documentation, artifact-classification rules, and recommendation logic can change as the example set drops some includes and adds agreement-scope values. R6 content remains structurally representable in R4 because R4 also allowed `CodeableConcept` with an example binding.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The risk is mainly artifact discoverability and filtering rather than direct patient data validity.

justification.inferredGoal: Refresh the example context-of-use vocabulary and add agreement-scope codes for CanonicalResource usage contexts.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base R6 datatype design is applicable because `value[x]` keeps the same shape and only an example-bound ValueSet compose changed.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Refreshing the example context-of-use vocabulary and adding agreement-scope content is a plausible R6 terminology goal. Because the binding remains `example`, the datatype choices, cardinality, and reference targets are unchanged, and base validation should not reject R4 instances solely because their codes are outside the revised example set. The missing change note prevents a stronger verdict, but the level of actual R4-to-R6 breakage is low.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The backward-compatible alternative question is not applicable to the base datatype: R4-valid `UsageContext.value[x]` content remains representable in R6. Keeping the old `use-context` includes while adding agreement-scope codes would be a less disruptive terminology curation choice for generated pick lists and business rules, but it is not needed to preserve R4 instance validity and could keep less-preferred example terminology in circulation.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Retaining old example includes could smooth UI and pick-list continuity, but it is terminology-curation continuity rather than a required base compatibility alternative and may preserve outdated suggestions.

evidence.detail: R4 binds `UsageContext.value[x]` to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/use-context` with example strength.
R6 retains the same value-set canonical and example binding strength for `UsageContext.value[x]`.
R4 `use-context` compose includes `usps-state` and `practitioner-specialty` among other external systems and value sets.
R6 `use-context` compose includes `v2-0265` and `usage-context-agreement-scope`, and no longer includes `usps-state` or `practitioner-specialty` by those canonicals.
The new R6 agreement-scope CodeSystem defines `realm-base`, `knowledge`, `domain`, `community`, `system-design`, and `system-implementation`.

examples.examplesMd: The example is illustrative of the R6 agreement-scope terminology pattern suggested by local R6 terminology descriptions. It is structurally representable in R4 because R4 `UsageContext` has the same `code` and `valueCodeableConcept` shape, but an R4 terminology-aware implementation may not recognize the newer agreement-scope semantics.

findings.narrativeMd: `UsageContext.value[x]` itself did not change shape, but the example-bound `use-context` ValueSet did. This affects systems that derive pick lists, generated constants, artifact indexing categories, or documentation from the example value set. Since the binding is only `example`, it should not produce a hard validation break for base instances.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A valid R4 instance using `valueCodeableConcept` should not become invalid in R6 just because its code is not in the changed example ValueSet, and valid R6 content can still be serialized in the R4 datatype shape. The compatibility risk is behavioral: validators may issue different informational messages, generated UI lists may add or remove choices, and business rules keyed to the R4 compose may miss new R6 agreement-scope values.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not transform `UsageContext.value[x]` structurally. Instead, refresh terminology expansion caches and review any code that assumes the R4 `use-context` compose. If systems use `valueCodeableConcept` for filtering or search facets, add tests covering removed R4 includes, the new `v2-0265` include, and the agreement-scope codes.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change may be appropriate terminology curation, but the supplied inputs do not explain why previous example includes were removed. Adding new agreement-scope content without removing old includes would have been easier for existing UI and rule engines, though it might have weakened the intended R6 guidance.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Expansion-level comparison was not performed. Some apparent compose removals may be offset by replacement value sets or overlapping external terminology expansions.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 and R6 keep `UsageContext.value[x]` with the same cardinality, choice types, reference targets, binding canonical, and example binding strength. The R6 `use-context` value set composition changes by removing some example includes and adding others, but an example binding is guidance for suggested terminology rather than a validation constraint. Existing R4 instances with values drawn from the removed example includes remain structurally valid in R6, and the R6 agreement-scope pattern is also representable in the unchanged R4 `CodeableConcept` shape. The direct effect is limited to pick lists, examples, or terminology suggestions.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition `UsageContext.value[x]`: min 1, max 1, choice types `CodeableConcept`, `Quantity`, `Range`, and specified `Reference` targets; example binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/use-context`.
R6 StructureDefinition `UsageContext.value[x]`: same cardinality, choice types, reference targets, binding canonical, and example strength.
R4 `ValueSet/use-context` includes `usps-state` and `practitioner-specialty` among other includes.
R6 `ValueSet/use-context` includes `v2-0265` and `usage-context-agreement-scope` and no longer includes those two R4 value set canonicals.
freshReview.fmmEffect: The supplied R4 maturity context is trial-use with unknown standards status, so terminology curation has less compatibility weight than it would for normative content. Because this is only an example binding, maturity does not turn it into a material break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: the example value set composition changes terminology guidance and possible UI suggestions, but it does not make old instances invalid or change generated element shape.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained the removed example includes while adding the new agreement-scope material, but that would be a terminology-curation choice with broader guidance tradeoffs, not a necessary compatibility-preserving base design. Since the binding is example strength, removal from the example set is not a meaningful break.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: I agree with the existing report's non-hard impact direction, but I place less weight on the proposed add-without-removal alternative because example-binding composition is not a constraining compatibility surface.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The R6 counterpart exists with the same canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, and abstract flag. Status/maturity changed and baseDefinition shifted, but those are handled as non-breaking metadata and out-of-scope infrastructure respectively.
Both snapshots contain the same local element set: `UsageContext`, `UsageContext.code`, and `UsageContext.value[x]`, plus inherited `id` and `extension`.
`valueReference` retains the same target profiles: `PlanDefinition`, `ResearchStudy`, `InsurancePlan`, `HealthcareService`, `Group`, `Location`, and `Organization`.
No local `UsageContext` invariant was added, removed, or changed. Snapshot differences in inherited `ele-1` XPath/condition metadata and `extension` constraints are base-artifact scope.
No fixed values, pattern values, or default values were found on the local elements in either version.
No local `minValue`, `maxValue`, `maxLength`, or regex constraints were found.
No local slicing is present in either StructureDefinition.

The root, `code`, and `value[x]` definitions are materially unchanged. Metadata description text changed from `Base StructureDefinition for UsageContext Type` to `UsageContext Type`, which does not alter datatype semantics.
No element name, choice base name, datatype choice, or reference target change alters JSON/XML serialization of local `UsageContext` instances.
No structural R6-only element or choice type was found, so R6 `UsageContext` instances are shape-compatible with R4. Semantic terminology differences may still require review for newer R6 codes.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Artifact status and standards maturity increased
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 `UsageContext` had StructureDefinition status `draft` and standards-status `trial-use`; R6 has status `active` and standards-status `normative`. This does not change instance validation or serialization.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance and documentation may treat the R6 datatype as more stable. This may affect policy decisions but not data transforms.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Publisher and jurisdiction metadata changed
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The publisher changed from `HL7 FHIR Standard` to `HL7 International / FHIR Infrastructure`, and R6 adds world jurisdiction metadata. These are StructureDefinition metadata changes, not instance content changes.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Systems that display or index specification metadata may see different publisher/jurisdiction labels.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds binding metadata extensions
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds binding-definition metadata and marks the `value[x]` binding as a common binding, but the local element shape and binding strength are unchanged.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tools that inspect ElementDefinition metadata may display richer binding documentation in R6.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: The R6 `UsageContext` baseDefinition is `DataType` instead of R4 `Element`. Per assignment scope rules, that class-hierarchy/base-artifact change should be handled by the base datatype analysis rather than this local report.
Inherited `id`, `extension`, and `ele-1` metadata differences appear in the snapshots but are inherited from `Element`/`Extension`, not local `UsageContext` changes.

The R6 `UsageContext.code` binding depends on this external THO ValueSet, which was not present in the local R6 core package. A terminology review should compare its expansion with the R4 `usage-context-type` CodeSystem.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff narrative was available in the local inputs, so rationale and intended migration behavior were inferred from computable artifacts.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the official FHIR change notes or datatype diff page for `UsageContext`.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 `usage-context-type` ValueSet is referenced by THO canonical but was not present in the local R6 core package, so exact R6 code additions/removals could not be confirmed.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Load the corresponding THO package or query a terminology server for `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/usage-context-type`.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The `use-context` comparison was based on ValueSet compose definitions, not fully expanded code sets. External value sets and filters may overlap in ways that reduce or amplify the practical change.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Expand both R4 and R6 `use-context` with the same terminology server and compare code/system/display membership.
